articles.title: AC Capacitor Bulging or Leaking? 60-Second Safety Check Before You Call

uniqueness_test.learn: The specific visual + audible symptoms of a failing AC capacitor (bulging top, leaking electrolyte oil, system trying to start then humming and shutting off), the 60-second LOOK-DONT-TOUCH protocol homeowners can safely run (kill the breaker, visual check from 3 feet, call), and the 4 things a technician checks on a capacitor service call (measured microfarad reading vs data-plate rating, voltage rating, weather sealing on the bottom, fan motor amp draw under load). Differs from live ac-contactor-clicking (contactor, not capacitor) and ac-compressor-buzzing-fan-not-spinning (mentions capacitor as one of multiple causes; this article is the deep-dive on JUST capacitor symptoms and the safety angle).
uniqueness_test.narrative_anchor: A bulging or leaking capacitor is the most catchable summer AC failure -- and the one with the highest DIY injury rate. Power off, look only, then call.
uniqueness_test.serp_overlap: Low. Symptom-specific safety angle. Queries like "ac capacitor bulging" / "ac capacitor leaking oil" / "is bulging capacitor dangerous" return contractor blogs and DIY forums -- no neutral aggregator covers the homeowner safety frame transparently.

articles.title: Heat Pumps in Cold Weather: The Physics (and Why Yours Still Works at 5F)

uniqueness_test.learn: The actual thermodynamics of heat-pump operation at sub-freezing outdoor temperatures: why coefficient of performance (COP) drops as outdoor temp drops but a cold-climate heat pump (CCHP) still moves more heat than electric resistance does even at 5F, what variable-speed inverter compressors and vapor-injection technology change about the cold-weather COP curve, the role of auxiliary/backup heat strips, the difference between balance-point heating and pure heat-pump heating, and the relevance of the EPA ENERGY STAR Cold Climate Heat Pump (CCHP) certification spec. Differs from the live 2026-heat-pump-buyers-guide pillar (purchase decision, not physics) and from article-heat-pump (general overview, not cold-weather specific).
uniqueness_test.narrative_anchor: Even at 5F outdoor, your heat pump is moving heat, not making it -- the physics works because there is still energy in the air above absolute zero, and a CCHP is engineered to harvest it efficiently.
uniqueness_test.serp_overlap: Low. Primary competitors are manufacturer pages (Mitsubishi Hyper-Heating, Bosch IDS) and the DOE Cold Climate Heat Pump page. Our angle: aggregator-honest, no brand bias, with the homeowner-decision frame layered onto the physics explanation. <40% overlap vs any existing site article.
